  principal, giving **20702.37** by the extended formula, and only then cancel the coverage — at

Two orders, two settlement figures and two terminal states, from sentences that are all in force.
`auto_ext_payoff_settlement.overwrite` is `[]` and

*F-C5 (the consent/owner boundary is reversed without declaration) — consequence demonstrated here.*
`auto_evt_gap_refund` is in force and says "cancelling is the borrower's own decision recorded
through an auto_requests row of request_type gap_cancellation that the borrower confirms", and
`blueprint.yaml` says for this difficulty that "payoff posting … [is an] agent service action" while
"GAP cancellation [is] the borrower's own instruction … completed by the borrower". The task tools
invert both: `post_gap_refund_16f4decd` is `owner="agent"` and writes no `auto_requests` row, and
`post_loan_payoff_a84c6454` is `owner="user"`. An agent reading the policy would hand the GAP
cancellation to the customer and post the payoff itself; the tool layer makes exactly the opposite
assignment, and `initial_state` seeds no `auto_requests` table, so the base sentence cannot be
satisfied by any available write. The persona is written to accommodate the tool layer rather than
the policy ("He is happy for the representative to make whatever entries the bank's rules require on
the loan first"), which conceals the contradiction at runtime but does not remove it from the
charter. **SOURCE-POLICY RED on task 1.**

### problem_chain

**The root the customer raises.** "I want to pay this car loan off in full today." That is
`auto_ext_payoff_settlement` (`subject: auto_payment`, `computes: settlement_amount`). He names no
prerequisite: `user_scenario` says "He offers no figures of his own", his knowledge of being behind
is unquantified ("he does not know how far behind, what has been added to the loan, or what interest
has built up"), and the GAP paragraph is explicitly conditioned on the agent raising it first ("If
the representative explains that the protection product financed with the loan has to be closed out
first…", and "if the representative never mentions the protection product he does not mention it
either"). No prerequisite is named or hinted at by the customer, and he asks for no extra item of
work — "He does not ask for a payoff letter, a receipt in the post or anything to be mailed to him."

**Nodes and edges derived from the rules.**

`auto_ext_payoff_settlement.rule` carries one prerequisite sentence:

> "The amount required to settle the loan in full is fixed only after the refund owed on the waiver
> coverage financed with the loan stands entered on its records."

State at `frozen_time`: `auto_loans[4f786106…].gap_coverage = true`, `gap_cancellation_date = ""`,
and `auto_transactions` contains no row with `event_type = auto_gap_refund` (the 31 seeded rows are
one `auto_disbursement`, 28 `auto_payment`/`scheduled` and two `auto_fee`/`late_charge`).
**False at the opening.** The only write in this difficulty that books a waiver-coverage refund
against the loan is `post_gap_refund_16f4decd`, the `target_tool` of
`auto_ext_gap_cancellation_refund`; no other tool touches `gap_coverage` or writes an
`auto_gap_refund` row. Edge → `auto_ext_gap_cancellation_refund`, kind `value_input` on
`principal_outstanding`.

`auto_ext_gap_cancellation_refund.rule` carries no prerequisite sentence; it is the leaf.

**Derived tree.** 2 nodes, root `auto_ext_payoff_settlement`, **1** prerequisite problem (inside the
1–3 bound), 1 edge, **1 `value_input`** (floor is max(1−1,1) = 1). No cycle.

**Topological order:** `auto_ext_gap_cancellation_refund` → `auto_ext_payoff_settlement`.

**Per-edge load-bearing run.** Skip `post_gap_refund_16f4decd` and replay: `principal_outstanding`
stays 20443.37 instead of 20053.37, the interest for 64 days at 5.99 % becomes 20443.37 × 5.99 / 100
/ 365 × 64 = 214.72 → 215.00 instead of 211.00, and `settlement_amount` becomes
20443.37 + 215.00 + 44.00 = **20702.37** instead of **20308.37**. The terminal state also differs:
`gap_coverage` stays `true` and `gap_cancellation_date` stays empty on a loan recorded as paid off.
**The edge bears weight.**

**Parallel edges.** None — the root has a single out-edge, so there is no ordering to resolve
between siblings.

**Owner=user write in the tree.** `post_loan_payoff_a84c6454` is `owner="user"` and the persona hands
it over on the agent's direction: "When the representative hands him the settlement to make himself,
he sends it for the figure he is told and reads the confirmation back." The requirement is met —
though see F-C5 above, which is about whether the charter *assigns* that owner, not about whether one
exists.

**No-wait argument.** Both resolving actions complete inside the call. The settlement is an
`external_ach` transfer the borrower sends on the line ("He will send the money from an account he
keeps at another bank, and he says so when he is asked how he wants to pay"); the tool posts it and
closes the loan in one synchronous write, and `auto_evt_payment_allocation`'s cutoff rule credits it
the same day at 14:05 ET on a Wednesday. The lien release is not a write of this task: the payoff
tool sets `lien_status="release_pending"` itself, and the base deadline
(`lien_release_business_days` = 10 business days after `closed_date`) is a future obligation, not a
prerequisite of anything here.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** Verified by reading the function bodies in
`env/regional_retail_bank/tasks/auto_loan_payment_servicing/task_tools.py`:
`post_gap_refund_16f4decd` creates the `auto_gap_refund` row and updates `gap_coverage`,
`gap_cancellation_date` and `principal_balance` unconditionally; `post_loan_payoff_a84c6454` creates
the `auto_payment`/`payoff` row and updates the loan unconditionally. Neither checks `gap_coverage`,
`status`, `days_past_due` or any other gate; the only conditional is the `if rows:` / `if
ctx.find(...)` guard against a missing holding row. No refusal, no error, no hint.

### task_independent_derivation

**Now / wait / refuse: act now.** `auto_evt_payment_allocation`'s eligibility `loan_open` allows a
payment on a loan whose `status` is `active` or `delinquent`; `status` is `delinquent`, so the payoff
posts. `auto_evt_delinquency` puts charge-off at `chargeoff_days_past_due` = 120 and
`days_past_due` is 63, so the loan is not charged off and the POLICY_NOT_COVERED carve-out for
charged-off balances does not apply. `auto_evt_gap_refund` allows cancellation "at any time while the
loan is open", and the loan is open. Nothing must wait.

**Authorisation and boundary.** "He is happy for the representative to make whatever entries the
bank's rules require on the loan first, and he says he will do his part himself if something has to
come from him." That authorises the agent's GAP entry and hands over the settlement. He wants it
today and not as a quote for a later date — "he wants it done on this call, not quoted for some later
date; he says so if he is asked whether he wants a figure for today or for a future date" — which
excludes the base `payoff_quote_valid_days` path. He asks for nothing beyond the settlement. The
persona closes exactly where the last write lands: "Once the representative tells him the loan is
settled and closed, he is plainly relieved and ends the call."

**Identity.** Phone 3365550588, DOB 1968-11-30, ssn_last4 1562, ZIP 27405 — all four match
`customers[fa341524…]`, so `find_customers` → `verify_customer_identity` with K=3 is satisfiable.

**Object.** The single auto loan `4f786106-e2c0-4d56-80c3-a442fa3fcd12`, a New Vehicle Loan on a
Honda CR-V, `status` delinquent, `days_past_due` 63, `principal_balance` 20443.37, `fees_due` 44.00
(two `late_charge` rows of 22.00 each, 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-31), `interest_rate` 6.24,
`monthly_payment` 694.07, `last_payment_date` 2026-06-14, `next_payment_due_date` 2026-07-15,

Correlated records: checking `012d60fe…` (Premier Checking, `ledger_balance` 3167.25, opened

### factor_weight

**Computation A — `refund_amount` (gold 390.00).**
Baseline from `baseline.rule` alone — "the refundable share is refundable_pct_standard percent of the
charge financed at funding, the months remaining are the term less the whole months since funding,
the unearned part is measured on the whole months remaining over the term, the cancellation fee is
the one the product publishes, and the refund is rounded half-up to the cent": refundable premium
795.00 × 90/100 = 715.50; months remaining 60 − 31 = 29; unearned 715.50 × 29 / 60 = 345.825;
less `gap_cancellation_fee` 50.00 = 295.825; rounded half-up to the cent = **295.83**. Definite, and
different from gold. `baseline.params` names `refundable_pct_standard`, the key its sentence uses;
the other defaults it relies on (`gap_cancellation_fee`, `term_months`) are the product's own
published figures, which the sentence names in words.

| factor | effect | tier taken | records putting the customer there | baseline this auditor computes | policy's declared `baseline` | scored value under it | bears weight |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| remaining_months_measure | method (which pair of dates spans the months) | middle ("from the installment then due to the scheduled maturity" = 31) | `checking_accounts[012d60fe…].ledger_balance` 3167.25 < 10000.00 (Premier Checking) **and** 3 ACH direct deposits ≥ 2 → exactly one holds (cross-difficulty: checking) | term less whole months since funding = 29 | `loan_term - MONTHS(F('funded_date'), NOW)` | 353.00 | yes |
| refundable_share_step | parameter (100 vs 95 vs 90) | middle (95) | 9 `auto_payment`/`scheduled` rows in 12 months, in [8, 12) | 90 | `K('refundable_pct_standard')` = 90 | 369.00 | yes |
| unearned_share_convention | method (days-over-days vs. ceil-to-quarter vs. months-over-term) | middle (ceil to the whole quarter: 31 → 33) | `checking_accounts.opened_date` 2021-05-20 → 63 months, in [48, 120) (cross-difficulty: checking) | months remaining over term | `refundable_premium * months_remaining / loan_term` | 365.00 | yes |
| cancellation_fee_step | parameter (0.00 vs 25.00 vs 50.00) | middle (25.00) | `card_accounts[8cf1fa33…].rewards_balance` 9800 in [5000, 25000); 7 card purchases in 3 months ≥ 3 (cross-difficulty: card) | the fee the product publishes = 50.00 | `P('gap_cancellation_fee')` = 50.00 | 365.00 | yes |
| refund_rounding | method (rounding point) | middle (half-up to the whole dollar) | `funded_date` 2024-02-09 → 31 months, in [24, 36) | half-up to the cent | `RND(refund_before_rounding, 2)` | 390.39 | yes |

Working: substituting one baseline at a time on the opening world.
`remaining_months_measure` → 755.25 × (int(29/3+…) ⇒ ceil-to-quarter of 29 is 30) × … = 755.25 × 30/60
= 377.625, less 25.00 = 352.625, half-up to the dollar = 353.00.
`refundable_share_step` → 715.50 × 33/60 = 393.525, less 25.00 = 368.525 → 369.00.
`unearned_share_convention` → 755.25 × 31/60 = 390.2125, less 25.00 = 365.2125 → 365.00.
`cancellation_fee_step` → 415.3875 − 50.00 = 365.3875 → 365.00.
`refund_rounding` → round(390.3875, 2) = 390.39.
Every one differs from 390.00.

Counts: 5 factors, 2 `parameter`, 3 `method`, 2 multi-source (`remaining_months_measure`,
`cancellation_fee_step`), 3 cross-difficulty (checking ×2, card). Bounds met.

`settlement_rate_step` → 20053.37 × 6.24/100/365 × 64 = 219.41 → 219.00 → 20316.37.
`settlement_transit_allowance` → days 66, interest 217.20 → 217.00 → 20314.37.
`settlement_interest_rounding` → 210.62 → 20307.99. Every one differs from 20308.37.

Counts: 4 factors, 2 `parameter`, 2 `method`, 3 multi-source (`settlement_clock_anchor`,
`settlement_rate_step`, `settlement_transit_allowance`), 3 cross-difficulty (checking, card ×2).
Bounds met.

**Cross-difficulty rows are actually seeded.** `checking_accounts[012d60fe…]` with 6
`checking_transactions`, and `card_accounts[8cf1fa33…]` with 12 `card_transactions`, are all present,
so every `XSUM` / `XCOUNT` / `CFIELD` / `CPARAM` returns a real value. The seeded rows agree with
their own charters: Premier Checking is a real tier with `waiver_min_daily_balance` 10000.00, and
Travel Rewards Visa Signature is a real card tier.

**Stamps.** No field of `auto_loans`, `checking_accounts` or `card_accounts` records a refundable
share, a months-remaining convention, a cancellation fee, a settlement rate, a transit allowance or a
rounding mode. Every tier is decided by an aggregate, a date span or a cross-category comparison the
rule describes.

**Near-miss records.** Present, but none of them flips a tier:

- `card_transactions` carries a **`card_payment`** of 3830.00 (2026-08-24) that a careless `XSUM`
  over `amount` would add to `card_year_spend`, giving 10780.00. The rule says "card purchases" and
  the compute filters `event_type='card_purchase'` — but 10780.00 is still inside [3000, 12000), so
  the `settlement_rate_step` tier does not move.
- The 2025-09-14 scheduled payment sits one day outside the twelve-month window (MONTHS = 12).
  Counting it gives `scheduled_paid_12m` = 10, still inside [8, 12), so
  `refundable_share_step` does not move.
- The 2026-05-19 card purchase sits outside the three-month window (MONTHS = 3). Counting it gives
  `card_purchases_3m` = 8, still ≥ 3 and still below `card_purchases_deep` 12, so
  `cancellation_fee_step` and `settlement_transit_allowance` do not move.
- The two `auto_fee` / `late_charge` rows (2026-07-31 and 2026-08-31, 22.00 each) make up
  `fees_due` = 44.00 exactly; no factor of either computation counts them, so a miscount there is
  not a near-miss for any ladder.

So this task's world contains records a careless reader would count and the rules exclude, satisfying
the letter of the requirement, but **not one of them changes a tier**, so no ladder in this task is
discriminated by score between a reader who applies the rule and one who counts by inspection.
Recorded as observation **T1-F1**.

## findings

---

**T1-F1 — observation — no near-miss in this task flips a tier.**

- *Symptom.* This world contains records a careless reader would count and the rules exclude — the
  3830.00 `card_payment` of 2026-08-24, the 2025-09-14 scheduled payment one day outside the
  twelve-month window, the 2026-05-19 card purchase outside the three-month window — but miscounting
  any of them leaves every ladder on the same tier, so neither computation's score distinguishes a
  reader who applies the rule from one who counts by inspection.
- *Evidence and consequence.* Worked out record by record in `source_derivation_frozen` →
  `factor_weight` → "Near-miss records": `card_year_spend` 6950.00 → 10780.00 stays inside
  [3000, 12000); `scheduled_paid_12m` 9 → 10 stays inside [8, 12); `card_purchases_3m` 7 → 8 stays
  inside [3, 12).
- *Affected artifact.* `initial_state` of task 1.
- *Relation to previous revisions.* New in revision 1.

---

**T1-F2 — SOURCE-TASK RED — the policy does not uniquely entail this task's two scored values or its
write order.**

- *Symptom.* Both scored parameters and the order of the two writes each have a second defensible
  answer derivable from base sentences that are in force and are rendered alongside the extended
  policies.
- *Root cause.* The undeclared overrides and the undeclared cross-problem order recorded as F-C1,
  F-C2 and F-C6 in
  `env/regional_retail_bank/audits/policy_task/auto_loan_payment_servicing/_difficulty.md` →
  `findings`. This is the consequence half; the findings themselves are charter-global.
- *Evidence and demonstrated consequence.* Set out against this task's world in
  `source_derivation_frozen` → `policy_self_consistency`:
  - `refund_amount`: base `auto_evt_gap_refund`'s pro-rata sentence gives 795.00 × 28 / 60 − 50.00 =
    **321.00**; the extended policy gives **390.00**.
  - `settlement_amount`: base `auto_evt_payoff_and_lien`'s payoff sentence with
    `auto_msr_accrued_interest` gives 20053.37 + 322.26 + 44.00 = **20419.63**; the extended policy
    gives **20308.37**.
  - the order: base `auto_evt_payoff_and_lien` ("A loan that is paid off with GAP coverage in force
    earns a GAP refund under auto_evt_gap_refund") and base `auto_evt_gap_refund` ("Paying the loan
    off early with GAP in force is treated as a cancellation on the payoff date") both put the payoff
    first, giving a settlement of **20702.37** and a refund entered against a loan already at zero
    principal; the extended prerequisite sentence puts the refund first, giving **20308.37**.
  None of the three base sentences is named in any `overwrite`, so all three are in force.
- *Affected artifact.* `auto.extended.yaml` →
  `extended_policies[auto_ext_payoff_settlement].overwrite` (`[]`),
  `extended_policies[auto_ext_gap_cancellation_refund].overwrite`,
  `policies[auto_evt_payoff_and_lien].rule`, `policies[auto_evt_gap_refund].rule`; the scored values
  at `evaluation_criteria[9].arguments.arguments.refund_amount` and
  `evaluation_criteria[11].arguments.arguments.settlement_amount`, and the step order 9 → 11.
- *Relation to previous revisions.* New in revision 1.

---

**T1-F3 — observation — `order_uniqueness` argues from gold rather than from policy.**

`tasks/1.json` → `prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness` excludes the reverse order with: "Taking the
settlement first would collect 20702.37 on a principal of 20443.37 and close the loan, after which
the refund entry would fall on a loan already at zero, so the terminal state differs from gold on the
loan row and on both ledger entries." Every figure in that sentence is correct — I derived 20702.37
independently — but "differs from gold" is the conclusion, not evidence for it, and the reverse order
is exactly what the two base sentences of F-C1 prescribe. Recorded as an observation because the
substantive defect is F-C1; this entry records that the artifact's own uniqueness argument does not
close the gap.

---

**T1-F4 — observation — `factor_sensitivity.tier_taken` states an "exactly one" tier as an "or".**

As in task 0 (T0-F6): `computations[0].factor_sensitivity[0]` and
`computations[1].factor_sensitivity[0]` describe the middle checking tier with "or" where the ladder
says "exactly one of those two holds", and the card ladders likewise. `factor_trace` states them
correctly ("so exactly one of the two holds"), and the tier taken is right in every case, so no value
moves.
